analysis.investment_thesis: Unified Data-Tech is a small-cap IT services company at ₹619 Cr market cap with healthy promoter holding of 60.39%, fitting the "Small" in SMILE. However, ROE of just 0.36% combined with a P/E of 21.10 makes it expensive with no evidence yet of the profitability transformation needed for a multibagger.
key_strengths: Small-cap sweet spot at ₹619 Cr market cap with information asymmetry opportunity
Strong promoter holding of 60.39% — adequate skin in the game
Low institutional coverage (FII 0.57%, DII 5.89%) — still undiscovered
key_risks: ROE of 0.36% is abysmal — well below my 15% threshold
P/E of 21.10 is expensive for a small-cap with weak profitability
Recently listed IT-ES player in a crowded, commoditized industry
red_flags: ROE 0.36% suggests either earnings collapse or inflated equity base post-IPO
P/E 21x on near-zero ROE is a valuation disconnect
analysis.detailed_analysis: On the SMILE framework, Unified Data ticks a few boxes — it is small (₹619 Cr), promoter-controlled (60.39%), and operates in IT services, a sector with a large TAM. But this is where the story breaks down. An ROE of 0.36% is a glaring red flag — either earnings have collapsed, or post-IPO equity dilution has bloated the denominator. Either way, at P/E 21.10 you are paying growth-stock multiples for a business earning almost nothing on capital. That is not a Kedia entry price.\n\nI want to see transformation — margin expansion, scale-up, a clear runway to 10x. Here the data gives me neither. IT-ES is a crowded space, and without differentiated IP or a niche leadership story, a tiny Mumbai integrator has no moat. I would keep this on the watchlist — revisit if ROE recovers above 15% and the market cap stays sub-₹1,000 Cr with a PE closer to 10-12x. Until then, no conviction for a buy.
